text:
maria: quick RFC follow-up: do we return an opaque resume bookmark string or a structured resume object from the service?
eli: ops question first: who owns persistence of the bookmark? client or server?
zane: client persists makes server simpler and lets us rotate internals. opaque string seems forward-compatible.
kai: opaque works but we need a clear retry & dedupe plan for partial page reads to avoid duplicates.
maria: two approaches: (1) at-least-once with client-level idempotency hints, or (2) server-side dedupe using session ids. both trade latency for complexity.
docs-bot: suggestion: add a short-lived "Grace-Period" header so reconnecting clients can resume without a new bookmark within X seconds.
eli: +1 to Grace-Period. SDKs can also optionally send Retry-Mode="session" and session-id when they have one.
maria: tentative SDK surfaces:
- simple: client.paginate(query, bookmark=None, retry_mode="auto")
- session: s = client.start_session(); s.paginate(...); s.bookmark()
zane: Session object is ergonomic for long jobs. keep simple stateless calls for quick use-cases. both supported.
kai: split responsibilities: transport-level retries handle short idempotent reconnects; SDK-level pagination handles resume/exponential backoff.
eli: defaults proposed: transport_backoff_initial=200ms, transport_backoff_max=2s, session_grace_default=5s.
zane: bookmarks should be base64url with opaque prefix (e.g., "bm:v1:") so we can rotate formats safely. avoid '+' and '/'.
docs-bot: telemetry events: session_start, session_resume, bookmark_issued, bookmark_used (include minimal metadata only).
maria: failure modes to document: bookmark expired -> 410 + Retry-From header; bookmark malformed -> 400. SDK to raise clear exceptions.
kai: implementers: question: should server accept both v1 bookmark string and v2 session object for backward compat?
maria: yes, server accepts both; SDKs to migrate to Session surface in v2 while keeping v1 compatibility.
eli: follow-up: language casing consistency - sessionId/bookmark/retryMode/gracePeriodMs and map to idiomatic casing per SDK (snake_case for python, camelCase for TS/Go).
zane: i'll mock a Python Session wrapper PR today. @maria can you open RFC PR with sample snippets for Python + TS?
maria: will do. TL;DR: expose opaque base64url bookmark, add optional Session surface, introduce Grace-Period header for short reconnects, separate transport vs SDK retry responsibilities, and wire minimal telemetry.
:thumbsup:
